title: Universal structure pushforward for product families
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-over-base]. For every $T\to S$ suppose the canonical units at $\mathcal O_T$ for tensor pullback along $f_T:X_T\to T$ and $g_T:Y_T\to T$ are isomorphisms [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Write $p:X\times_S Y\to S$ for the product family [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then for every $T\to S$ the canonical unit at $\mathcal O_T$ for tensor pullback along $p_T:(X\times_S Y)_T\to T$ is an isomorphism. No flatness or finiteness hypotheses are required.

source.place: Tag 0BF3, product-family hypotheses for applying Tag 0BF2; elementary pullback-pasting proof

proof.text: Use Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app to compare the chosen tensor adjunction with the ordinary pullback adjunction. Compose with pushforward of the pullback-of-unit isomorphism. This yields SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit, whose components are the underlying ring maps a.app U. Evaluation detects an isomorphism, and conversely pointwise inverses assemble by PresheafOfModules.isoMk and fully faithful forget. Thus the unit is an isomorphism iff all a.app U are.

Pullback symmetry and pasting identify the product over T with Y pulled back to T×_S X. The composite of that projection with T×_S X→T equals the original product map after this isomorphism. Both projections satisfy the open-section criterion by the hypotheses. Hom.comp_app and preservation of isomorphisms prove the criterion for the composite and hence the desired unit isomorphism.
